editorialNote: Independent interpretive study notes, not A.A. headings or official text. Page numbers indicate useful starting points; they are not verified sentence-level boundaries. No book text is included.

entries.label: Drinking grows beyond Bill's control
entries.note: The early story develops loss of control and the narrowing options of alcoholism.

entries.label: Willpower and promises fail
entries.note: Resolve, fear, and consequences are not enough to sustain sobriety.

entries.label: A new spiritual possibility
entries.note: Ebby's visit opens a different approach: Bill need not accept somebody else's fixed conception of God.

entries.label: An inward change begins
entries.note: Bill's account shifts toward a spiritual experience and a new outlook.

entries.label: Carry the message onward
entries.note: The narrative moves from personal change to helping others.

entries.label: A shared experience of recovery
entries.note: The fellowship offers a common experience rather than another isolated attempt to quit.

entries.label: The real alcoholic distinguished
entries.note: The book separates heavy drinking and ordinary choices from the loss of control it is describing.

entries.label: No reliable mental defense
entries.note: Knowledge and memory of earlier disasters may fail at the decisive moment.

entries.label: A solution beyond self-control
entries.note: The argument turns from failed personal defense to the possibility of a profound change.

entries.label: An invitation to examine the approach
entries.note: The reader is invited to consider the spiritual basis described in the next chapter.

entries.label: Conceding powerlessness
entries.note: Denial and the desire to drink normally occupy the opening discussion.

entries.label: Experiments in control
entries.note: Strategies for regulating alcohol are tested and found unreliable for the alcoholic.

entries.label: The peculiar mental blank spot
entries.note: Personal stories illustrate how the first drink can appear reasonable despite consequences.

entries.label: What the cases have established
entries.note: The accumulated stories lead toward the admission that self-knowledge is not a sufficient defense.

entries.label: Defense must come from a higher power
entries.note: The chapter closes by pointing beyond the individual's own resources.

entries.label: The book's major turn: diagnosis to remedy
entries.note: The first three chapters described the dilemma. Here the book explicitly introduces the spiritual remedy.

entries.label: Lack of power
entries.note: The central dilemma is described as a shortage of power, rather than a shortage of information.

entries.label: Begin with your own conception
entries.note: The barrier is lowered: an initial willingness to believe can be a beginning.

entries.label: Old ideas and prejudices block the way
entries.note: Fixed assumptions are examined as obstacles to a new experience.

entries.label: Look within and become willing
entries.note: The chapter calls for openness and a search for a spiritual foundation.

entries.label: Willingness and honesty matter
entries.note: The chapter opens by stressing the conditions under which the approach has worked.

entries.label: From surrender to the Twelve Steps
entries.note: The writing crosses from admitting failure into a specific program of action.

entries.label: Self-will in the director's chair
entries.note: The actor analogy shows how attempts to manage everyone and everything produce conflict.

entries.label: Self-centeredness identified; reliance introduced
entries.note: The text makes a sharp diagnosis and then redirects the reader toward a different source of help.

entries.label: Third Step decision
entries.note: The remedy becomes an actual decision and a stated commitment.

entries.label: Make a searching inventory
entries.note: The Fourth Step moves the change from intention into written examination.

entries.label: Resentment examined differently
entries.note: Attention moves from other people's conduct to the reader's own part and response.

entries.label: Face fears directly
entries.note: The inventory turns to fear, its causes, and a different response.

entries.label: Examine relationships and conduct
entries.note: The inventory expands to sex and personal relationships.

entries.label: Prepare to tell the truth
entries.note: The Fifth Step brings inventory into a conversation with another person.

entries.label: After confession, into readiness
entries.note: The narrative pivots from disclosure to preparation for further change.

entries.label: Six, Seven, Eight, and Nine become concrete
entries.note: Readiness, asking for help, and making amends lead into specific conduct.

entries.label: Results of making amends
entries.note: The text describes the changes expected from doing this work.

entries.label: From repair to daily maintenance
entries.note: After the promises the program becomes an ongoing practice of inventory and correction.

entries.label: Conscious contact as a daily practice
entries.note: Prayer and meditation are described as practices rather than abstractions.

entries.label: Service stabilizes recovery
entries.note: Helping another alcoholic becomes central to continued growth.

entries.label: Approach another alcoholic practically
entries.note: The chapter gives concrete instructions about how to make contact.

entries.label: Do not push or preach
entries.note: The message is to be offered without pressure or arguments.

entries.label: Let the other person choose
entries.note: The approach changes from persuading someone to respecting their readiness.

entries.label: Practice the principles in ordinary life
entries.note: Carrying the message connects back to responsibilities at home and work.

entries.label: The family's experience of alcoholism
entries.note: The chapter introduces the harm and confusion experienced by partners.

entries.label: Control and argument often backfire
entries.note: Attempts to force a change in the drinker may intensify conflict.

entries.label: A new approach for the partner
entries.note: The discussion turns toward understanding, restraint, and constructive responses.

entries.label: Make room for rebuilding trust
entries.note: Rebuilding life requires practical care beyond merely stopping alcohol.

entries.label: Recovery is not instant repair
entries.note: Families may need time and patient action even after drinking stops.

entries.label: Sobriety doesn't fix every family difficulty
entries.note: A changed drinking pattern does not automatically erase old habits or hurt.

entries.label: Recovery becomes a family process
entries.note: The focus shifts to mutual change, patience, and shared responsibility.

entries.label: Progress rather than perfection at home
entries.note: Everyday behavior, balance, and humility matter more than grand promises.

entries.label: Rebuild ordinary family life
entries.note: Attention returns to recreation, relationships, and responsibilities.

entries.label: Keep expectations proportionate
entries.note: Old conflicts can return; spiritual progress is an ongoing practice.

entries.label: The workplace sees only the damage
entries.note: Employers confront absence, broken trust, and behavior they cannot easily explain.

entries.label: Punishment alone misses the illness
entries.note: Routine discipline does not necessarily address alcoholism's underlying nature.

entries.label: A constructive, informed response
entries.note: The chapter turns toward understanding alcoholism and offering a realistic chance.

entries.label: Set fair expectations and boundaries
entries.note: Support includes responsibility and sound decisions, not permissiveness.

entries.label: Recovery can restore useful workers
entries.note: The chapter offers a practical reason for employers to consider another approach.

entries.label: The old life narrows to isolation
entries.note: The last chapter begins by returning to alcohol's hopeless cycle.

entries.label: The larger possibility appears
entries.note: The writing turns from what drinking has cost to the life recovery may open.

entries.label: Fellowship replaces isolation
entries.note: Shared identification and a common purpose are presented as powerful changes.

entries.label: The message spreads through service
entries.note: The story of the movement emphasizes practical help and connection.

entries.label: An open-ended vision of usefulness
entries.note: The book closes by directing attention toward continued growth and service.
